column4: This verse says neither dust nor humiliation covers the good-doers' faces and names them as Garden companions; its own contribution is the uncovered, protected face opposite the darkened face in 10:27 and the section's opposed outcomes.
The fire is described as reaching the hearts (تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ); this is a specific inner reach for the section's image of an outer cover working inward to thought.
The Fire is closed over its people (مُّؤْصَدَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ); it is a direct enclosing punishment, the oppressive counterpart to the Garden's protective covering.
The enclosing fire is held by extended pillars; this verse gives the physical form of the closure stated in 104:8, adding how its covering is fixed around them.
The section names the Ghashiya covering root; here people cover themselves with their garments to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and reveal, joining an outer cover to inward secrecy.

The section's J-N-N dictionary branch defines a shield as something that protects; this verse says people use their oaths as a shield while turning others from God's way, a deceptive protection unlike the Garden's refuge.
The same shield phrase recurs: the hypocrites take their oaths as a shield and then turn away from God's path; it repeats the section's protective J-N-N branch in a false, concealing use.
God teaches David to make armor that protects people from their violence; this is a concrete shield-like covering and gives the section's protective Garden cover a bodily counterpart.
A parable describes a Garden on high ground that yields double produce after heavy rain; the high, fruitful Jannah connects the section's elevated Garden to growth under a covering soil.
After the smoke covers people in 44:11, they plead for the punishment to be removed; this verse contributes the afflicted people's response to that specific cover.
The God-fearing are placed in a secure abode (مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ), the refuge side of the same surah whose smoke covers people in 44:11; it contrasts safety with an enveloping punishment.
God protects the Garden people from the punishment of Hell (وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ); it repeats the section's defining contrast between protection and punishment.
The day is sworn by when it displays; this verse supplies the daylight boundary to the night-cover in 91:4, and its own contribution is the revealed side of that pair.
The day is sworn by when it appears (وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ); it completes the night-covering in 92:1 with the image's opposite, daylight made manifest.
The night is made dark and the day luminous as paired signs; the verse develops the boundary between obscuring night and visible day that the section traces through night-cover images.
The parable layers darkness in a deep sea, with wave over wave and cloud above, until a person can scarcely see a hand; it gives a specific, layered cover that reaches sight.
God's speech can come from behind a veil (مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ); this is a distinct, non-punitive use of concealment that marks a boundary of perception beside the section's enveloping cover.

The section's H-M-Y dictionary branch describes protected grazing land; the verse names the Hām as an animal treated as reserved by custom. If that name carries the same protection sense, it contrasts human-declared protection with the section's protection from scorching punishment.
The Garden of the right hand has extended shade (وَظِلٍّ مَّمْدُودٍ); this is a direct tree-covering refuge that gives the section's garden shelter a concrete form.
The Garden's shade hangs close over its people and its fruit is brought low; this develops the section's protective tree-cover as an enclosing, accessible shelter.
The Garden promised to believers includes deep shade (ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا); it states the sheltering quality of the section's reward in another direct Garden scene.
The Garden's people and spouses rest in shade; this makes the Garden a place of shelter, extending the section's image of a covering that protects.

The wrongdoers are screened from their Lord on that Day (لَمَحْجُوبُونَ); its own contribution is exclusion by a veil, opposite the Garden's protecting cover, after the prior verse describes hearts obscured by their deeds.
A garden of date palms and grapes is struck by a fiery whirlwind and burned; this is a concrete reversal of the section's Garden as a shelter from scorching punishment.
The verse identifies the dust-covered faces in 80:40–41 as the disbelieving wicked (الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ); it links the covered face to the section's K-F-R branch of truth-covering.

People hurry out from their graves on the Day like racers to a marker; this gives the movement into the humbled-eye and overwhelming humiliation scene in 70:44, paralleling the section's judgment-day gathering.
